title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Price Label & Markdown Sticker. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Price Label & Markdown Sticker
options.lineage: Korean mart and Japanese konbini / depachika shelf labels
options.thesis: Every expense wears its split like a supermarket sticker slapped on the price.
options.viewport: Balance printed as a red label band at top; today's entries as shelf labels with big condensed prices; a round split sticker on each; thumb-reach Add button.
options.risk: Can tip into novelty if the stickers multiply beyond the one job they do.

raised.raise: Amounts set on a fixed magnitude ramp: a 2 000 kr hotel reads bigger than a 40 kr coffee at a glance.
Sticky guide header names the days in view and their running total while the list scrolls.
Sync state is line form, not hue: an unsynced entry's sticker is dashed until the server confirms it.
Editing expands one label in place and dims the rest of the shelf.

options.label: Metro Line Map
options.lineage: Seoul Metro and Tokyo Metro line maps and station numbering
options.thesis: Each of you is a line colour; every expense is a station on the trip's route.
options.viewport: Balance as two coloured lines converging on a settle point; entries as stations down a vertical route with day interchanges.
options.risk: Transit maps are the first thing most travel apps reach for; familiar more than distinctive.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: One yellow band always shows the next decision: who owes whom, and what to log next.
options.viewport: A monumental balance on a yellow band; entries as black rows with pictogram categories.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity; travellers know it, but it's the airport, not Seoul or Tokyo.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere fatigues when the band stops being reserved for one job.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain words, and one bright colour that only appears where you can act.
options.viewport: Balance card on top, expense cards stacked, persistent bottom bar with Add.
options.case: Holds clarity and comfort; loses on identification, nothing in it is about this trip.
options.risk: Pleasant and anonymous; looks like every budgeting app.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Expenses as stars sized by magnitude.
options.case: Loses both axes: nobody splits a bill under a red flashlight.
options.kept: Fixed magnitude ramp for amount size.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder & Plate
options.thesis: The trip as a dictionary of entries.
options.viewport: Dense text columns with guide words.
options.case: Loses both axes: too bookish for one-handed logging at a till.
options.kept: Guide words: a sticky header naming the span in view.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: State as line form on one rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract where money needs to be literal.
options.kept: Pending vs confirmed shown by dashed vs solid line, not colour.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Expenses as tiles in horizontal rows.
options.case: Loses both axes: horizontal rows hide the one number that matters.
options.kept: Focus expands one item and dims the rest.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Splitwise-style expense splitter, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Balance summary at top, chronological expense list, floating add button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps you already know by design.
